turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_supercon_train.csv: 300 real materials, columns `composition`
    (element fractions as a compact formula string) and `target` (the
    measured critical temperature Tc (K)).
  - b3_supercon_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE materials whose critical temperature
    Tc (K) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and `composition`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST critical
temperature Tc (K), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data show that the highest Tc materials are layered cuprates, especially Hg/Tl/Bi-based systems with multiple CuO₂ planes. Among the pool, the candidates most consistent with those highest-Tc families are:

- c029: Ag/Cu–Ba–Ca–Cu–O high-Tc cuprate, analogous to Cu/Tl–Ba–Ca–Cu–O (training Tc ~115 K).
- c084: Hg/Bi-stabilized Sr-1223 cuprate, analogous to Hg/Pb–Ba–Ca–Cu–O (training Tc ~118 K).
- c034: Tl-based multilayer cuprate with high Ca/Cu count, analogous to Tl–Ba–Ca–Cu–O superconductors.
- c097: Bi/Pb–Sr–Ca–Cu–O, close to training Bi1.6Pb0.3Te0.1Sr2Ca3Cu4O (Tc ~102.7 K).
- c046: Mo-doped Bi-2223 cuprate, related to Bi/Pb–Sr–Ca–Cu–O high-Tc phases.

Final: c029, c084, c034, c097, c046
